5355.idn: Name in the source: lɔŋto [lɔ̀ŋtó]; Lɔ̀ŋtó; voko (Voko); speakers: Lɔŋmo (Lɔ̀ŋmó ou Lɔ̀ŋvɛ); family in the source: Lɔŋto appartient au groupe Duru, rameau de Samba-Duru. Samba-Duru est un groupe de langues de la famille 'Benue-Volta'

tn.quote: La langue lɔŋto a trois hauteurs tonales: haut, moyen et bas. Il y a aussi deux tons descendants: haut-bas et rarement moyen-bas. En général les sons qui portent les tons sont les voyelles, et parfois /l/ ~ /r/ et les nasales /m/ ~ /n/ et /ŋ/ s'ils sont les seuls sons d'un morphème ou en position finale d'un mot ou morphème. ... En général les tons descendants sont exclusivement prononcés à la fin d'une phrase. ... Donc, toutes les voyelles qui sont sans marque de ton sont prononcées moyens.
tn.translation: The Lɔŋto language has three tone heights: high, mid and low. There are also two falling tones: high-low and, rarely, mid-low. In general the sounds that bear the tones are the vowels, and sometimes /l/ ~ /r/ and the nasals /m/ ~ /n/ and /ŋ/ if they are the only sounds of a morpheme or in final position of a word or morpheme. ... In general the falling tones are pronounced exclusively at the end of a sentence. ... So all vowels without a tone mark are pronounced mid.
tn.cite: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich (avec l'assistance de Illiassou Godje et Bouba Bakary). 2012 [digital edn 2021, 'Dictionnaire lɔŋto ACAD 1.0']. Lexique Lɔ̀ŋtó (~ Voko) - Français. Poli: Lamido de Voko / Comité de Développement du Lamidat de Voko / DFG. 68 pp.
tn.locator: p. 4, section 1.2 'Le ton'
tn.note: Three level tones (H, M, L) plus falling HL and rare ML, the falls only phrase-finally; long vowels written double may carry two different tones; infinitives never begin with L. Nothing on stress.

evidence_works.work: Patman 1991, Tone in the Nugunu verb phrase (SIL Cameroon typescript = Nugunu chapter of Anderson (ed.) Tone in five languages of Cameroon, SIL/UTA PL 102: 22 pp.)
evidence_works.detail: A first-hand tonological description: sec. 1.0 Introduction states 'Nugunu has two phonemic tones, H and L. These may be realized at any number of phonetic pitch levels because of the process of downdrift, in which the pitch of any H tone following a L is lower than the pitch of preceding H tones. Rising, falling, and rising-falling contours are also found, formed by the juxtaposition of two or more dissimilar tones.'. The paper then posits tone rules for the verb phrase (sec. 2.0 ff.). It contains no statement about stress or accent: the only hit for 'accent' is the orthographic note that the paper marks H and L tones with accents. No elicitation procedure or consultant is described.

L'impossibilité de trouver sur un monosyllabe une opposition entre trois tons ponctuels dont aucun ne soit le résultat d'une neutralisation nous a fait considérer que le wori est une langue à tons normalement ponctuels, au nombre de deux. Ces deux registres fondamentaux, haut et bas, donnent quatre possibilités distinctives ... ce qui ne doit pas faire conclure à l'existence de 4 tons en wori, mais signifie seulement que la succession des deux tons ponctuels de cette langue dans le cadre d'une même syllabe a valeur distinctive.
tn.translation: Wori is a tone language. ... The impossibility of finding on a monosyllable an opposition between three level tones none of which results from a neutralisation led us to consider Wori a language with normally level tones, two in number. These two basic registers, high and low, give four distinctive possibilities ... which must not lead one to conclude that there are 4 tones in Wori, but means only that the succession of the two level tones of this language within one syllable is distinctive.
tn.cite: Hagège, Claude. 1967. Description phonologique du parler wori (sud-ouest du Cameroun). Journal of West African Languages 4(2): 15-34.
tn.locator: p. 15, II 'Les tons', Introduction (first sentence); p. 17, II 2 Interprétation (rest)
tn.note: Two level tones (high, low) on every vowel and syllabic nasal; HL and LH on one syllable analysed as two morae, not extra tonemes; L is mid before H or between two H (allotones); nothing on stress.

Nominals can be elassified into four tone-groups according to the tone of the radical and suflix. ... 4.4. An acute accent (’) marks a high tone, and an unmarked syllable denotes a normal low tone. tn.quote: Sarwa is a three tone level language:5 à low, ā mid, á high. In addition, various contour tones exist, such as â high–low, a᷄ mid–high, a᷆ mid–low, e. g. ndû “locust”, nàrâ “persons”, ndǝ̀mâ “sheep”, nju᷄ “goat”, ŋgīrīm̀ “crocodile”. ... Sarwa verbs can furthermore be grouped into tone classes which are independent from, and cross-cut with the ablaut class ... in its tonal equipment, the two level outfit typical of the east has already increased to a three level system.
tn.cite: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2021. A Sketch of Sarwa, a Chadic Minority Language in Central Chad. Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenländischen Gesellschaft 171(1): 9-37.
tn.note: Three level tones L M H; contours HL, MH, ML also occur, named as level combinations (open list, not counted). Verb tone classes M-HL, H-HL, L-L. Fn 5: Abdoul 2016 saw two levels. Nothing on stress.

evidence_works.work: Dell 1981, La langue bai: phonologie et lexique (Paris: Éditions de l'EHESS; chap. 2 'Système phonique du bai de Da-li', sec. 2.4 'Le système tonal', pp. 29-34)
evidence_works.detail: Describes the 'bai de Da-li' of a single consultant from a locality near Dali (p. 21); the entry's Wang 2006 table describes Zhoucheng (ZC), whose consultant was born in Zhoucheng village (Wang 2006 p. States that every syllable carries a tone as necessary to its identity as the initial or the final, and that there is no position in the chain where all tonal distinctions are neutralised, unlike the Pekingese 'neutral tone' ('Chaque syllabe porte un ton, aussi nécessaire à son identification que l'initiale ou la finale. Il n'existe pas dans la chaîne de position où toutes les distinctions tonales sont neutralisées, comme dans le cas du "ton neutre" du pékinois.', p. 29). Distinguishes pre-pausal (PP) syllables (before a pause or major syntactic break, incl. monosyllables and final syllables of polysyllables in isolation) from non-pre-pausal (NPP) syllables: eight tones in PP syllables, seven in NPP where T3 and T4 merge ('Le système tonal présente un paradigme de huit unités en syllabe PP, et de sept seulement en syllabe NPP, où les tons 3 et 4 sont confondus.', p. 29). T7, long low and inflected (212/211) in isolation, is realised whenever preceded by another syllable as a low punctual tone 'qui donne une impression auditive semblable à celle du "ton neutre" pékinois lorsqu'il suit une syllabe au quatrième ton' (p. 32): an auditory resemblance to a neutral tone, explicitly not a neutralisation. Instrumental part: on 68 isolated monosyllables recorded by G.K.C., rhyme duration measured from release of the initial to the last glottal pulse varies by tone nearly threefold ('la durée de la finale varie presque du simple au triple selon le ton', p. 33), the three level tones lying midway. 8-43.
evidence_works.loc: p. 29, T7 remark p. 32, duration measurements p. 33, discussion continuing on p. 34

5375.idn: Name in the source: Kunda (name given by their Angbandi neighbours; self-designation riverains 'Isó bábale', Babale); Motémbó; family in the source: riverains bantu; 'sous-groupe Motembo' (1. Kunda, 2. Babale 'Bapoto', 3. Motembo)

tn.quote: Il existe deux tons de base bas et haut. Cette tonologie présente un certain nombre de spécificités qui ne paraissent pas être claires: elle est déplacée par endroits aussi bien au milieu qu'au début de la phrase. ... Ce qui est clair est que les substantifs ont généralement un ton haut sur le PN. Ceux qui comportent un augment ont un ton haut sur celui-ci et le PN porte un ton descendant (bref ?) là où on s'attendrait à un bas. ... Existent deux tons de base (bas et haut), avec possibilités d'obtenir des tons doubles (descendant et montant).
tn.translation: There are two basic tones, low and high. This tonology shows a number of peculiarities that do not seem clear: it is displaced in places, both in the middle and at the beginning of the sentence. ... What is clear is that nouns generally have a high tone on the nominal prefix. Those that carry an augment have a high tone on it and the nominal prefix bears a (short?) falling tone where one would expect a low. ... There are two basic tones (low and high), with the possibility of obtaining double tones (falling and rising).
tn.cite: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale. (Études Æquatoria, 8.) tn.note: Two basic tones, low and high, in Kunda and Motembo; falling/rising treated as compound tones; tone 'displaced' vs Lingala-type in places; elided vowel's tone shifts to next syllable; no stress data.

5376.idn: Name in the source: Le tupuri; Tüpürï, /jäãk tüpürï/ ‘langue toupouri’; noms alternatifs: tüpürï, toupouri, toubouri, tpuri; family in the source: famille Niger-Congo, embranchement Adamawa-Oubangui, branche Adamawa, groupe 6 Mbum, sous-groupe Northern

tn.quote: Le tupuri est une langue à quatre hauteurs tonales. Les paires minimales sont imparfaites. Les consonnes obstruantes sonores et continues ont provoqué un abaissement tonal qui donne lieu à un ton infra-bas. ... Le ton mi-bas provient de l’abaissement d’un ton mi-haut d’un schème mi-haut mi-bas. Les voyelles fermées après consonne sourde tendent à élever le registre mi-haut jusqu’à un registre haut. ... La structure syllabique étant en syllabe ouverte, en contexte, le timbre d’une voyelle finale est élidé, le ton de cette syllabe étant amalgamé aux tons de la syllabe qui suit.
tn.translation: Tupuri is a language with four tone heights. Minimal pairs are imperfect. Voiced obstruents and continuants caused a tonal lowering that gives rise to an infra-low tone. ... The mid-low tone comes from the lowering of a mid-high tone of a mid-high mid-low scheme. Close vowels after a voiceless consonant tend to raise the mid-high register up to a high register. ... Syllable structure being open, in context the quality of a final vowel is elided, the tone of that syllable being merged with the tones of the following syllable.
tn.cite: Ruelland, Suzanne 2010. Le tupuri. Sorosoro (Pour que vivent les langues du monde), language page 'réalisée par Suzanne Ruelland' (LACITO/LLACAN), published 2010-07-15, updated 2010-08-19; section 'Précisions linguistiques' + 'Sources & bibliographie'. https://www.sorosoro.org/le-tupuri/
tn.locator: web page, section 'Précisions linguistiques'
tn.note: Four level tone heights (high, mid-high, mid-low, infra-low), extremes described as arising from consonant/vowel conditioning; labels gathered from prose, no table; no forms with tone labels shown. Checked against the source (tone consistency check, 2026-09-23): evidence impressionistic -> alternations (web page, section 'Précisions linguistiques').

corr.words: Ce phénomène s’observe dans les formes verbales injonctives, où les verbes ayant une consonne sourde à l’initiale ont un schème tonal mi-haut mi-haut, tandis que les verbes à l’injonctif ayant des consonnes sonores à l’initiale ont le schéma infra-bas mi-haut. Le ton mi-bas provient de l’abaissement d’un ton mi-haut d’un schème mi-haut mi-bas. ... La morpho-tonologie permet aussi d’élucider la création de quatre hauteurs tonales.

tn.quote: L'examen de la flexion vocalique de /a/ combinée avec celle des trois tons ne permet pas de donner aussi facilement des traductions dégagées de tout contexte. Dressons d'abord un tableau des variations formelles. [table: MOYEN HAUT BAS] Les six formes obtenues ne sont pas indépendantes les unes des autres. Elles ne présentent pas des oppositions individuelles de façon ponctuelle; mais /a/ et /e/ s'opposent pour chacun des trois tonèmes selon le champ (b); moyen s'oppose à bas et haut selon le champ (d), et haut à bas selon le champ (f).
tn.translation: Examining the vocalic inflection of /a/ combined with that of the three tones does not so easily allow translations free of all context. Let us first draw up a table of the formal variations. [table: MID HIGH LOW] The six forms obtained are not independent of one another. They do not present individual oppositions in a point-by-point way; rather /a/ and /e/ are opposed for each of the three tonemes according to field (b); mid is opposed to low and high according to field (d), and high to low according to field (f).

variants.name: !Xóõ, Lone Tree-Kagcae dialect (as described by Traill; formerly filed under the code of East Taa)
variants.prule: Lexical tone language: four tones (high, mid-level, mid-falling, low) carried by the stem, written on its first vowel; the stem (root) is the tone domain, prefixes and suffixes lie outside it. No word-stress or accent rule is stated in any first-hand source opened; Downing 2004 reports finding no discussion of stress in the Khoisan literature.
variants.quote: Considerations of legibility have dictated that tone marks and nasalization are normally not marked on one vowel. Thus it seems that in a word like !á̰ã only the second vowel is nasalized and only the first vowel carries a tone and is pharyngealized whereas the phonetic transcription of this word, namely [!ã̰́ː], shows that there is actually a single high-toned, long, nasalized and pharyngealized vowel. [...] Vowels are also distinguished by tonal differences and it has been necessary to impose an ordering on vowels that differ only tonally. The arbitrary ordering is as follows (using a for illustration): a (high)- a (mid-level) - a (mid-falling) - a (low). [...] Plural suffixes and noun prefixes are consistently separated from the stem with a hyphen. This not only marks the morpheme divisions involved, but also delimits the domain of the stem tone. The fact that a prefix, stem and suffix constitute a grammatical word is also captured by the hyphenated structure.
variants.loc: Traill 1994 Introduction sec. 3.5 'The order of items with the same initial consonant', pp. 12-13, and sec. 6 'Hyphens and morphological divisions', p. 15; Downing 2004 sec. 4 pp. 111-112 (pp. 11-12)
variants.cite: Traill, Anthony. 1994. A !Xóõ Dictionary (Quellen zur Khoisan-Forschung 9). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. Introduction, secs. 3.5 and 6. Corroborating survey: Downing, Laura J. 2004. What African languages tell us about accent typology. ZAS Papers in Linguistics 37: 101-136, sec. 4 pp. 111-112 (publisher PDF, reporting Traill 1985).
variants.cfw: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 7 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
variants.note: Filed under the code of East Taa (huaa1248) until V9.20; the description is of !Xóõ, Lone Tree-Kagcae dialect, a variety of West !Xoon (xooo1239). '!Xóõ' (the source language, Traill 1994 A !Xóõ Dictionary) is an alternative name of BOTH huaa1248 East Taa (elcat: !Ko, !Xuun, !Xóõ, Taa, Tsasi...) and its sister xooo1239 West !Xoon (Tuu > Hua > Taa (2)); name search '!Xóõ' returns both.

tn.quote: Vowels are also distinguished by tonal differences and it has been necessary to impose an ordering on vowels that differ only tonally. The arbitrary ordering is as follows (using a for illustration): á (high)- ā (mid-level) - â (mid-falling) - à (low). ... This not only marks the morpheme divisions involved, but also delimits the domain of the stem tone. ... The lexical tone of the noun is independent of the tonal melody asociated with a noun. Thus one can find examples of any of the four lexical tones with either of the two melodies.
tn.cite: Traill, Anthony. 1994. A !Xóõ Dictionary (Quellen zur Khoisan-Forschung / Research in Khoisan Studies 9). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. 292 pp.
tn.locator: sec. 3.5 'The order of items with the same initial consonant (complex)' p. 12; sec. 6 'Hyphens and morphological divisions' p. 15; sec. 10.3 'Tone classes for nouns' p. 23
tn.note: Four lexical tones (high, mid-level, mid-falling, low) on the stem, written on its first vowel; affixes lie outside the stem-tone domain. Nouns also have Tone Class I/II concord melodies; verbs H/M/L.

5380.idn: Name in the source: Yateé Zapotec (yate1242; zty); family in the source: a variety of Northern Core Zapotec belonging to the Otomanguean language family

tn.quote: Yateé Zapotec has four tones: High (V́), Low (V̀), Rising (V̌), and Falling (V̂); and three phonations: Modal (V), Checked (Vˀ), and Rearticulated (VˀV). Each phonation can bear any of the four tones (Example 1). Not every pair of words in Example (1) form a minimal pair. However, we managed to find words whose nucleus is /a/ for every tone-phonation combination. ... when the imperatives and the past tense cannot be distinguished by phonation, a tone change is observed, suggesting that tone be used with a grammatical function in the language.
tn.cite: Chai, Yuan, Adrián Fernández & Briseida Mendez. 2024. The role of phonation and tone in TAM in Yateé Zapotec. Paper presented at the Annual Meeting of the Society for the Study of the Indigenous Languages of the Americas (SSILA), January 2024. 2-page abstract.
tn.locator: abstract p.1, para. 2 (before Example 1); last sentence from p.2, final paragraph
tn.note: Four tones (High, Low, Rising, Falling) fully crossed with three phonations; tone also marks TAM (low->falling in IMP vs PST). Data from primary fieldwork; no TBU or stress statement.
